system.summary: Numeric groups of 2-4 digits separated by full stops, set inside clear letters. Most groups split into two numbers of 2-24 (2210 = 22|10, 912 = 9|12); the editors of 1824 printed them as figures because they had no key.
system.notes: Same system in both writers' letters (shared groups 199, 515, 129, 814, 1220), so it is probably Duplessis's cipher with his Paris correspondents in 1593.

prior_solution.where: The 1824 editors (vol. 6 p. 82 note) printed figures they could not read; web search 25 Oct 2026 found no later decipherment.

conditions.human_role: Asked for a target that needs no archive request; chose this one.

solution.what: Searched the full text of all 12 volumes (archive.org) for chiffre/déchiffré and runs of figures. Mme de Rohan's 1594 letter (vol. 6 LVI) is printed with its decipherment above the figures; Du Maurier and Serviez 1593 (vol. 5), Loménie 24 Feb 1595 (vol. 6 CVII) and Duplessis 1597-98 (vols. 7-8) are printed as bare figures.
Transcribed the eight 1593 passages (93 groups, 62 distinct) from the page images with their clear context (ciphertext.txt).
Split each group into two numbers of 1-24; both halves draw on the same set of values, suggesting each half stands for a letter (a bigram per group).

anneal_pairs.py: number->letter key annealed onto fr-1600-letters (order 4, no spaces) with a French letter-frequency penalty, 10 restarts. No restart produced French; the bigram-per-group reading is not supported at this length.

Built the Mme de Rohan 1594 key (78 values) from the decipherment printed above her figures, vol. 6 pp. 83-85 (rohan1594_key.tsv): letters 6-65, syllables 88-175, word codes 660-919 including 810 = de and 910 = les, and names 10 = le roi, 87 = Paris, 95 = Tours, 96 = Saumur.

Transcribed Loménie to Duplessis, 24 Feb 1595 (15 passages, vol. 6 pp. 179-181), Duplessis to his wife 1595 (vol. 6 p. 182) and Duplessis to Cargroy and to his wife, 18-19 Jan 1597 (11 passages, vol. 7 pp. 124-126) from the page images.

Applied the Rohan 1594 key to the 1595 and 1597 figures. The output does not make French: most groups have no value, and those that do give place names and letters in the middle of words. The key is not the one used in these letters. One partial fit: in Loménie, 'du sieur 810 62 110 4' reads as 'du sieur de ...', so the word-code series ending in 10 may be shared even though the letter values differ.

gaps.detail: Pairs anneal failed; no key found.
The Rohan 1594 key does not fit. Vols. 7 (later 1597 letters) and 8 (1598) are not yet transcribed.
